A Short Field Guide to Lighthouses

By morning the oil is low and the keeper is tired. The lamp is
put out at sunrise, the curtains are drawn against the day, and
the brass is polished before breakfast.

Chapter 2: Keeping the Log
Every keeper writes in the log. The entries are plain: the hour
the lamp was lit, the state of the sea, the direction of the wind
and the number of ships that passed.
A good log is boring. When a page has only weather on it, the
night went well. The pages that people read years later are the
other ones, written in a hurried hand, with a blot where the
pen was put down too fast.
The log is kept in a tin box under the stairs, wrapped in oilcloth, because paper and sea air are old enemies.
